 By Tuba Zahra October 28, 2026 Share 3 Min Read SHARE Summary
 Cricket fever is building in Adelaide as Australia prepares to host New Zealand for the much-anticipated Christmas Test, with a unique promotional campaign putting two of the home team’s biggest stars in the spotlight.
 With just 50 days remaining before the festive cricket showdown, giant images of Australian batters Travis Head and Alex Carey have been unveiled in Adelaide, drawing attention to the upcoming series and adding to the city’s excitement.
 The giant portraits of Head and Carey have already helped turn the city into a promotional stage for the upcoming Test, signalling that the festive cricket season is drawing closer.
 AI Generated Summary Cricket fever is building in Adelaide as Australia prepares to host New Zealand for the much-anticipated Christmas Test, with a unique promotional campaign putting two of the home team’s biggest stars in the spotlight.
 With just 50 days remaining before the festive cricket showdown, giant images of Australian batters Travis Head and Alex Carey have been unveiled in Adelaide, drawing attention to the upcoming series and adding to the city’s excitement.
 Cricket Australia organised the special event to mark the countdown to the Test, which is scheduled to take place from December 17 to 21 at Adelaide Oval. The campaign celebrates the two cricketers, who have strong connections to South Australia, and aims to build anticipation ahead of the international contest.
 Head’s wife, Jess Head, and their children attended the unveiling ceremony, making the occasion a family celebration as well as a promotional event for Australian cricket. Former Australian cricketers Mel Jones and Callum Ferguson were also present, adding further star power to the gathering.
 The striking displays have brought cricket into the public eye across Adelaide, offering residents and visitors a visual reminder that one of the summer’s major sporting events is approaching.
 The Christmas Test is expected to be a significant fixture in Australia’s home international calendar, with New Zealand arriving to challenge the hosts in the traditional five-day format. The contest will provide both sides with an opportunity to test their skills in front of Australian supporters during the busy festive season.

By featuring familiar local sporting figures in prominent city displays, organisers are creating a sense of occasion around the match and encouraging supporters to look forward to the December encounter.
 With the countdown now underway, anticipation is growing for the Australia-New Zealand battle in Adelaide. The giant portraits of Head and Carey have already helped turn the city into a promotional stage for the upcoming Test, signalling that the festive cricket season is drawing closer.
